posts.content_md:
Crown hologram ( video and picture ) shot with JDS Hene laser on Ultimate 08 plate.

Exposure time 11 sec.

![Image](http://www.myfilestash.com/userfiles/tirex/Crown%202.jpg)

[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l8H1E86IG8U](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l8H1E86IG8U)

posts.author: bernardb
posts.content_md:
Beautiful!

Since I am relatively new, may I ask what power the laser, wavelength, model?

Also, is this a "single beam" kind of hologram?

Very Very nice!

posts.author: Kris Meerlo
posts.content_md: It is a singlebeam reflection hologram shot with a 20mw JDS 1145P polarized HeNe laser ( 633 nm ).

posts.author: bernardb
posts.content_md:
Cool! 

I have one of those too (1145P)...I just need the TIME to get off my butt and start actually making holograms instead of researching *how* they are made...

Thanks again!

(PS - where did you buy the Ultimate 08 from?)

Oh, one more thing, how large is the plate?, and how large is the actual crown object?

posts.author: Kris Meerlo
posts.content_md:
The plates are from [http://www.ultimate-holography.com/](http://www.ultimate-holography.com/)

 And the size is about 4 by 5 inch ( 10 by 13cm ) the crown is a little bit smaller.

posts.author: bernardb
posts.content_md:
Thank you!

Very clear nice hologram...expensive plates, but worth it for the quality I guess...

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
> **bernardb:** Thank you!Very clear nice hologram...expensive plates, but worth it for the quality I guess...

If you are trying to save money, learn to do processing on pfg-01 first as there are many mistakes to be made. When you can make them clean then switch to Ultimate or BB-640. If money is no object then starting with a more expensive plate will shorten the learning curve.
